name: Crowhurst Yew

official_register.name: Ancient Yew Group database (Tim Hills 1997 to 2004 survey, Peter Norton re-measurements)

access: Free. Open public churchyard (AYG: access public; protection and responsibility Parochial Church Council unless stated).
how_to_recognise: Grows ENE of St George's church, near the east end. Hollow trunk with a low door-like opening (4 ft high) in the bole, chains and props.
verify_notes: AYG 385: 1003 cm at 122 cm (Hills 9 Jul 1999); Peter Norton 2013: 32 ft 11 in (1003 cm) at 4 ft; Richard Cooper 2008: 10.06 m at 1.45 m, 10.37 m at 30 cm. Documented since 1630: parish record says 10 yards round in the time of Charles I; Evelyn, Aubrey, Brayley 1850 (10 yd 9 in at 5 ft), Lowe 1890 (32 ft 6 in at 5 ft; the larger of the Surrey and Sussex Crowhursts). Hollow: about 1820 the vicar had a door fitted and a bench and table put inside it (seats ten to fourteen); a 7 lb cannonball was found in or embedded in the trunk, supposed Civil War. Choir sang inside it 1825 (Stamford Mercury). Roof of the hollow fell in by 1850. Swanton 1955 thought it unhealthy; Hills 1999: two gaps in the bole, much dead wood, chain swallowed by new wood, door 4 ft high. Alive: Norton 2013 re-measurement; Commons file of the yew dated Sep 2024 (Geograph 7894661, GPS 51.209241,-0.010474, about 10 m from the AYG pin; lifecheck RECENT 2024-09-28). Church earliest parts 12th century. Do not confuse with Crowhurst, East Sussex (also in this file: Lowe discusses both). Age: DERIVED from the AYG girth class (7 m and over is probably over 800 years); not a dating, popular claims are recorded in the notes where a page says them. name: Tandridge Yew

official_register.name: Ancient Yew Group database (Tim Hills 1997 to 2004 survey, Peter Norton re-measurements)

access: Free. Open public churchyard (AYG: access public; protection and responsibility Parochial Church Council unless stated).
how_to_recognise: At the west end of St Peter's church. Huge hollow, split trunk mass with a vast spreading crown, fluted branches and younger yews growing around it.
verify_notes: AYG 765: 1092 cm at 5 cm (Hills 9 Jul 1999), a ground-level figure over a fluted, split mass; older girths at 5 ft: about 30 ft (Brayley 1850), 32 to 37 ft across 1880 to 1999 per the AYG grid. Tall as well as stout (Hills: many straight fluted branches, a canopy circle of 250 ft per a 1936 source). Hollow, cavity darkened by fire or smoke; main stem fractured long ago with two great lateral trunks (Lowe 1890: 10 ft and 13 ft 4 in). Reported dying in 1831 and 1850, recovered strongly (1936 and 1958 sources). Younger yews nearby probably layered from the parent. AYG notes a second Notable yew (id 3392) with no data. Alive: Hills 1999 and AYG file of 2025; Commons/Geograph photos of the yew include 7296752 (22 Sep 2021, GPS 51.242788,-0.031808) and 8049419 to 8049422. Church earliest parts Norman. Girth is the ground figure, treat as multi-stem mass. verify_notes: AYG: 915 cm (Hills 7 Jul 1999; Norton re-measured 2015), twin trunk: each trunk about 16 ft (about 490 cm) at 1999, both fluted and hollow, 'the healed halves of a single stem' (Johnson, Sussex Tree Book 1997); massive low base, trunks slant apart, props and chains in place, windswept spreading crown. name: Corhampton Yew

official_register.name: Ancient Yew Group database (Tim Hills 1997 to 2004 survey, Peter Norton re-measurements)

access: Free. Open public churchyard (AYG: access public; protection and responsibility Parochial Church Council unless stated).
how_to_recognise: Tall female yew in the churchyard of the Saxon church: clean, visible bole, big branches reaching across the path and into the ground, one support left.
verify_notes: AYG: 732 cm near ground (Hills 18 Sep 1998); 1999 Hills 23 ft 4 in at ground (711 cm) and 25 ft 1 in at 3 ft; Russell Cleaver 1999 7.11 m at 1.1 m; Peter Norton 2010 24 ft near ground, 23 ft 6 in at 5 ft; Steve Waters 2011 716 cm at 1.4 m. Earliest record an early 18th-century watercolour owned by the church; travel writers 1865 and 1897 praise it. Female, tall, clean visible bole, large leading branch and a second, dividing at about 7 ft; branches spread across the path and root where they touch the ground; originally 15 props, one now. Healthy green foliage 1999. Late Saxon church founded 1020, built on an artificial mound. Church has no dedication. Alive: Norton 2010/2011 and Waters 2011 re-measurements; Commons has 'Corhampton Yew.jpg' and 'Corhampton yew trunk.jpg'; AYG file of 2020. Last dated evidence 2011, so flagged. verify_notes: AYG 349: 721 cm at 90 cm (Hills 6 Jul 1999: 23 ft 8 in); Peter Norton 23 May 2013: 23 ft 5 in at 3 ft 6 in, on the north side. name: Coldwaltham Yew

location.address: St Giles's Church, Coldwaltham, West Sussex

official_register.name: Ancient Yew Group database (Tim Hills 1997 to 2004 survey, Peter Norton re-measurements)

access: Free. Open public churchyard (AYG: access public; protection and responsibility Parochial Church Council unless stated).
how_to_recognise: NW of St Giles's church: a very large completely hollow bole with two straight fluted branches rising from it; a notice names it among the oldest yews.
verify_notes: AYG 366: 1049 cm at 15 cm (Hills 4 Jun 1999, 34 ft 5 in); Peter Norton 2012 also 34 ft 5 in and 30 ft 9 in at 3 ft; 1955 35 ft at ground and 32 ft at 3 ft; Johnson 1997 14 m tall, 296 cm diameter. Regarded as Sussex's senior veteran yew (Johnson, The Trees of Sussex). A female, NW of the church: two straight fluted branches rise from the bole, a central branch closing around old growth, a large limb removed. Completely hollow with major basal cavities, many nails hammered into the bole; crown thinner in 2012 than in 1999 (AYG). AYG calls the 3000-year age in Meredith's gazetteer unsupported, and 'one of the oldest twelve' on a notice is possible but unlisted. Norman church rebuilt in the 19th century. Alive: Norton Jun 2012 photos; flagged, last dated evidence 2012 and a thinning crown; no named Commons photo found. location.address: St Andrew's Church, Tangmere, West Sussex

official_register.name: Ancient Yew Group database (Tim Hills 1997 to 2004 survey, Peter Norton re-measurements)

access: Free. Open public churchyard (AYG: access public; protection and responsibility Parochial Church Council unless stated).
how_to_recognise: South of St Andrew's church: stout female yew with a leaning section held by chains as the main branch.
verify_notes: AYG: 808 cm at 30 cm (Hills 15 May 1999); Norton 2011: 26 ft 6 in at 1 ft, 24 ft 4 in at 3 ft (below 3 ft distorted by trunk growth); 1848 20 ft at a yard; 1988 24 ft 8 in at 3 ft (letter to David Bellamy); Johnson 1997 12 m tall, 232 cm diameter. Female, grows south of the church; a leaning chained section carries the main branch; new wood is laid down on the inner surface. The churchyard was told in the 1760s the yew was dead and another was planted in its place; the replacement failed and the old yew recovered. Illustrated London News Feb 1846 and Church Builder 1885 ('the finest in all the country round'). Saxon church replaced about 1100. Alive: Norton 2011 photos, 'fine healthy female' 1999; flagged, last dated evidence 2011, no named Commons photo found.
